Name: Fishtown Tavern
Description: Easygoing Frankford Ave neighborhood bar with American pub fare, weekend brunch, and a laid-back local crowd.

Name: Johnny Brenda's
Description: Beloved Fishtown institution at Frankford & Girard — a gastropub with local beer and elevated bar food downstairs and a legendary live-music venue upstairs.

Name: Pizza Shackamaxon
Description: Neighborhood Fishtown pizza joint for a quick, no-fuss slice.

Name: Bok Bar
Description: Rooftop atop a former South Philly high school with incredible skyline views, weekly events, and a rotating chef residency. Kid-friendly before sunset, dog-friendly always. Seasonal, mid-April through October.

Name: Irwin's
Description: Eighth-floor Italian patio in the Bok Building. Book around sunset and order the gnocchi sardi, tiramisu, and plenty of Italian wine.

Name: Assembly Rooftop Lounge
Description: Atop the Logan Hotel with Parkway views, cocktails, and small plates. Cozy fire pits in winter, and a prime perch for July 4th fireworks and the Thanksgiving parade.

Name: Stratus Lounge
Description: Chic, high-walled rooftop in Old City’s Hotel Monaco. A great weekend spot (Thursday–Saturday) for cocktails, small plates, and DJ sets.

Name: Sunset Social
Description: Constant lawn-party vibe on the Cira Green rooftop park. Always kid- and dog-friendly, with outdoor movies, quizzo, DJ dance parties, and yappy hours.

Name: Continental Midtown
Description: 1960s-vibe Stephen Starr rooftop with heat lamps, occasional DJ sets, and the famous Tang-dusted Astronaut martini.

Name: El Techo
Description: Retractable-roof rooftop above Condesa — good even in iffy weather. Mezcal margaritas and “All of the Salsas.” 21+ except Sunday brunch.

Name: Attico Rooftop & Bar
Location: 219 South Broad St, Avenue of the Arts
Description: Sixteen floors above the Avenue of the Arts at the Cambria Hotel — a plant-filled indoor-outdoor oasis with small bites, weekend brunch, and Friday/Saturday DJ sets.

Name: Balcony Bar at Kimmel Center
Description: The Kimmel Center’s second-tier balcony, open summer Wednesdays for Center City Sips. Grab a selfie with City Hall behind you and a hot dog in hand.

Name: Revolution House
Description: Second-floor Old City deck with a retractable roof. A sun-drenched weekend brunch is the move.

Name: Emmy Squared
Description: Rooftop Detroit-style pizza, sandwiches, and really good drinks — a solid date spot.

Name: PHS Pop-Up Gardens
Description: The original Philly pop-up beer garden. Food, craft brews, cocktails, plant swaps, and craft workshops — plus a frozen Gritty Marg. South St location and a Manayunk “urban forest” spot with a game room.

Name: Parks on Tap
Description: A traveling beer garden popping up across city parks over 27 weeks. Room to roam, burgers and hot dogs, and a portion of proceeds benefits each park.

Name: Frankie's Summer Club
Description: Beer garden in the courtyard of former UArts’ Furness Hall, with food and a must-try soft-serve by Irwin’s and backyard-party vibes.

Name: Jet Wine Bar
Description: A wine garden, not a beer garden — comfortable, casual, and colorful with global wines and shareable Mediterranean and Spanish bites.

Name: Walnut Garden
Description: 11,500-sq-ft Rittenhouse beer garden, kid- and dog-friendly, with cheesesteaks, chicken sandwiches, game-day big screens, and a mini playground.

Name: Attic Brewing Company
Description: Germantown brewery with a dog- and kid-friendly beer garden out back, a full schedule of food trucks, and live music and comedy.

Name: Rodin Garden Bar
Description: Summer-Friday bar in the Rodin Museum’s oasis-like courtyard among eight Rodin sculptures, with live music and a food truck. Kid- and dog-friendly.

Name: Uptown Beer Garden
Description: Center City spot across three bars with ever-changing themes — tiki in summer, spooky at Halloween, Santa’s Workshop for the holidays.

Name: Evil Genius Beer Co.
Description: Fishtown brewery (the “Lab”) with a delightful, colorful beer garden, whimsically named beers, and Friday off-leash Yappy Hours.

Name: Independence Beer Garden
Description: 20,000-sq-ft Michael Schulson space across from the Liberty Bell with a big beer list, wings, fried pickles, TVs, and outdoor games like shuffleboard and cornhole.

Name: Frankford Hall
Description: Year-round Fishtown German biergarten with giant soft pretzels, schnitzel, and bratwurst. The huge outdoor area stays warm with heat lamps and fire pits.

Name: Cherry Street Pier
Description: Open-air riverfront space with Ben Franklin Bridge views, a pop-up bar, artist galleries, art installations, and craft markets. Seating is first-come, first-served.

Name: Spruce Street Harbor Park
Description: The waterfront classic with the floating Lazy Hammock bar, reservable hammock lounges, a 16-ft video wall, and a full summer concert lineup.

Name: Morgan's Pier
Description: Seasonal Delaware River hotspot with DJs, specialty cocktails, several outdoor bars, family-friendly weekend brunch, and monthly Yappy Hours.

Name: Liberty Point
Description: Massive outdoor restaurant at the Independence Seaport Museum — three levels, five bars, panoramic waterfront views, and live entertainment.

Name: Fringe Bar
Description: FringeArts’ outdoor beer garden — a calmer waterfront option with weekend Pumphouse Pizza, brunch, and Ben Franklin Bridge views.

Name: Southwark
Description: A hidden-gem Queen Village courtyard adorned with flowers and herbs — many of which end up in the menu.

Name: Caletta
Description: Poolside patio at Fishtown’s boutique hotel Anna & Bel. Go for aperitivo hour (Wed–Fri, 4–7pm) when every drink comes with a snack.

Name: Royal Boucherie
Description: A hidden upstairs terrace in Old City that doesn’t feel like Philadelphia — oysters and rosé that feel like a mini vacation.

Name: El Chingon Fishtown
Description: The casual, summery Fishtown offshoot of chef Carlos Aparicio’s award-winning spot, with an outdoor “Jardin de Agave” and its own bar.

Name: Wm. Mulherin's Sons
Description: A dreamy outdoor dining spot with plants, twinkle lights, and picnic tables, serving spritzes and wood-fired pizzas.

Name: Front Street Cafe
Description: Fishtown’s all-day cafe with a tucked-away back garden and an outdoor bar — perfect for day-drinking.

Name: Suraya
Description: A beautiful 5,000-sq-ft Levantine courtyard framed by Persian ironwood trees, with its own bar so the cocktails keep flowing.

Name: Sor Ynéz
Description: Laidback Kensington Mexican spot with a cute enclosed patio and a working garden that flavors the dishes. Bonus: lots of free parking.

Name: Le Virtù
Description: Elegant East Passyunk Abruzzese spot with an ample, partially covered patio, homemade pastas, an antipasti board, and an olive-oil martini.

Name: Osteria
Description: Beyond the glass-enclosed patio is a dreamy pergola — graze on antipasti, sip something light, and catch the great weekend happy hour.

Name: American Sardine Bar
Description: Point Breeze stalwart with a string-lit lot next door — lawn chairs, beer, tinned-fish samplers, and salt-and-pepper fries.

Name: Talula's Garden
Description: Washington Square farm-to-table spot beloved for its cheese plate and extra-fresh everything. The rustically planted courtyard seats are coveted.

Name: Parc
Description: The quintessential Rittenhouse Square sidewalk brasserie. Order a seafood tower and a spritz and get your people-watching on.

Name: Harper's Garden
Description: Edison-bulb string lights and lush greenery make this open-air veranda a lovely spot for a spritz or frosé after work.

Name: Booker's Restaurant & Bar
Description: West Philly comfort, brunch, and happy hour — Southern favorites like fried chicken and waffles under a plant-filled Baltimore Ave pergola.
